cards.title: Jesus Fashioning Live Birds from Clay in Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2
cards.note: Surah 3:49 presents Jesus declaring to the Sons of Israel that he will fashion the form of a bird from clay and breathe into it so that it becomes a living bird, matching the clay sparrows miracle in chapter 2 of the second-century Infancy Gospel of Thomas.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators state that the Quran preserves an authentic miracle from the childhood and ministry of Jesus that was left unrecorded in the four canonical Gospels.
discussion.reply: First-century New Testament writings contain no account of Jesus animating clay birds, and John 2:11 explicitly identifies turning water into wine at Cana as the first of His signs. The clay birds narrative first appears in the mid-second-century Greek Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2, alongside episodes of the child Jesus withering and striking down playmates.

cards.quranEn: And (He will make him) a messenger to the Sons of Israel. ‘Surely I have brought you a sign from your Lord: I shall create for you the form of a bird from clay. Then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird by the permission of God. And I shall heal the blind and the leper, and give the dead life by the permission of God. And I shall inform you of what you may eat, and what you may store up in your houses. Surely in that is a sign indeed for you, if you are believers.
quranHighlights: I shall create for you the form of a bird from clay. Then I will breathe into it and it will become a bird

sources.en: And having made some soft clay, He fashioned out of it twelve sparrows. And it was the Sabbath when He did these things. And there were also many other children playing with Him. And a certain Jew, seeing what Jesus was doing, playing on the Sabbath , went off immediately, and said to his father Joseph: Behold, your son is at the stream, and has taken clay, and made of it twelve birds, and has profaned the Sabbath . And Joseph, coming to the place and seeing, cried out to Him, saying: Why do you do on the Sabbath what it is not lawful to do? And Jesus clapped His hands, and cried out to the sparrows, and said to them: Off you go! And the sparrows flew, and went off crying. And the Jews seeing this were amazed, and went away and reported to their chief men what they had seen Jesus doing.

cards.title: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 After Cain and Abel: Saving or Killing One Soul
cards.note: Surah 5:32 moves directly from Cain killing Abel in 5:27–31 to a decree for the Sons of Israel that killing one person is like killing all mankind and saving one is like saving all mankind, matching the rabbinic homily on Genesis 4:10 in Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God revealed this legal principle to the Children of Israel in their ancient scriptures following the first human murder.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Genesis 4:10 records the narrative of Cain and Abel without any decree equating one life to all mankind. That maxim originates in Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (c. AD 200), where rabbinic sages explicitly derive it as human courtroom commentary on the plural Hebrew word for bloods (demei) in Genesis 4:10.

cards.quranEn: From that time We prescribed for the Sons of Israel that whoever kills a person, except (in retaliation) for another, or (for) fomenting corruption on the earth, (it is) as if he had killed all the people. And whoever gives (a person) life, (it is) as if he had given all the people life. Certainly Our messengers have brought them the clear signs, yet even after that many of them act wantonly on the earth.

sources.en: Therefore, Adam the first man was created alone, to teach you that with regard to anyone who destroys one soul from the Jewish people, i.e., kills one Jew, the verse ascribes him blame as if he destroyed an entire world, as Adam was one person, from whom the population of an entire world came forth. And conversely, anyone who sustains one soul from the Jewish people, the verse ascribes him credit as if he sustained an entire world.

cards.title: Pharaoh Ordering Haman to Bake Clay Bricks and Build a Tower to Heaven
cards.note: Surah 28:38–42 portrays Pharaoh in Egypt ordering Haman to bake clay bricks and build a lofty tower to climb to the God of Moses, combining the baked-brick tower of Babel (Genesis 11:3–4; Sanhedrin 109a) with Haman from the Persian court of Esther 3:1.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators and modern harmonizers propose that Haman was either an unrecorded Egyptian court minister or a title of an Egyptian quarry official distinct from the Persian vizier in the Book of Esther.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Haman the Agagite serves King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) in fifth-century BC Persia (Esther 3:1), roughly a millennium after Moses and Pharaoh in New Kingdom Egypt. Furthermore, firing clay bricks in a kiln to build a tower reaching the heavens is the specific architectural motif of Mesopotamia's Tower of Babel in Genesis 11:3–4 rather than Egyptian stone masonry.

cards.quranEn: [38] Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses. Surely I think he is indeed one of the liars.’ [39] He and his forces became arrogant on the earth without any right, and thought that they would not be returned to Us. [40] So We seized him and his forces, and tossed them into the sea. See how the end was for the evildoers! [41] We made them leaders (who) call (others) to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. [42] We pursued them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the scorned.
quranHighlights: Pharaoh said, ‘Assembly! I know of no other god for you than me. So light a fire for me, Haman, on the clay, and make a tower for me, so that I may look at the god of Moses.

cards.title: Talut (Saul) Testing Troops at the River Like Gideon Before Slaying Goliath
cards.note: Surah 2:249–251 attributes to King Talut (Saul) the river-drinking test of Gideon's army from Judges 7:4–7—separating those who drink freely from those who scoop water by hand—immediately before David slays Jalut (Goliath) as in 1 Samuel 17:48–51.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain this passage either as a separate unrecorded test conducted by King Saul on the march to face Goliath or as an intentional prophetic parallel between two Israelite campaigns.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, the river test separating three hundred men who scoop water with their hands from the rest of the army belongs to the judge Gideon fighting the Midianites (Judges 7:4–7). King Saul's campaign against the Philistines and David's slaying of Goliath occur generations later in 1 Samuel 17, where no river-drinking test takes place.

cards.quranEn: [249] When Ṭālūt set out with his forces, he said, ‘Surely God is going to test you by means of a river. Whoever drinks from it is not on my side, but whoever does not taste it is surely on my side, except for whoever scoops (it) up with his hand.’ But they (all) drank from it, except for a few. So when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him, they said, ‘We have no strength today against Jālūt and his forces.’ But those who thought that they would meet God said, ‘How many a small cohort has overcome a large cohort by the permission of God? God is with the patient.’ [250] So when they went forth to (battle) Jālūt and his forces, they said, ‘Our Lord, pour out on us patience, and make firm our feet, and help us against the people who are disbelievers.’ [251] And they routed them by the permission of God, and David killed Jālūt, and God gave him the kingdom and the wisdom, and taught him about whatever He pleased. If God had not repelled some of the people by means of others, the earth would indeed have been corrupted. But God is full of favor to the worlds.

cards.title: Dhu l-Qarnayn Building the Iron and Molten Brass Gate Against Gog and Magog
cards.note: Surah 18:92–98 depicts Dhu l-Qarnayn erecting a rampart of iron blocks and molten brass between two mountain cliffs to seal in Gog and Magog until the apocalyptic promise of the Lord, matching the sixth-century Syriac Alexander Legend.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as Ibn Ishaq, al-Tabari, and al-Qurtubi identify Dhu l-Qarnayn as Alexander the Great (`al-Iskandar`) or a righteous world-conqueror who built an iron-and-brass barrier in the north.
discussion.reply: Historical records of Alexander of Macedon (356–323 BC) show a polytheistic Greek king who built no apocalyptic wall against Gog and Magog. The plot of a two-horned monotheistic king traveling to the ends of the earth and casting an iron-and-brass gate between two mountains against Gog and Magog was composed in Syriac in northern Mesopotamia shortly before Islam.

[94] They said, “Dhū-l-Qarnayn! Surely Yajūj and Majūj are fomenting corruption on the earth. Shall we pay tribute to you on (the condition) that you construct a barrier between us and them?” [95] He said, “What my Lord has established me with is better. Help me with a force, (and) I shall construct a rampart between you and them. cards.title: Mary Beneath the Date-Palm Fed by Dropping Dates and a Miraculous Stream
cards.note: Surah 19:22–25 depicts Mary resting exhausted beside the trunk of a date-palm, where a voice from beneath her commands a water stream to flow at her feet and bids her shake the palm trunk for fresh ripe dates, matching Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew 20.

discussion.view: Classical exegetes regard this scene as a divinely revealed account of Mary's solitary childbirth in the wilderness near Bethlehem.
discussion.reply: Canonical Luke 2:4–7 places Jesus's birth in Bethlehem with Joseph present, without a palm tree or water spring. The combined miracle of the date-palm bending its fruit to Mary and a spring opening from its roots appears in chapter 20 of the sixth-century Latin Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew during the Holy Family's later flight into Egypt.

She said, ‘I wish I had died before (this) and was completely forgotten!’ [24] And then he called out to her from beneath her, ‘Do not sorrow! Your Lord has made a stream beneath you. [25] Shake the trunk of the date palm toward you, and it will drop on you fresh ripe (dates).

sources.title: Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew
sources.en: Then the child Jesus, with a joyful countenance, reposing in the bosom of His mother, said to the palm: O tree, bend your branches, and refresh my mother with your fruit. And immediately at these words the palm bent its top down to the very feet of the blessed Mary; and they gathered from it fruit, with which they were all refreshed. And after they had gathered all its fruit, it remained bent down, waiting the order to rise from Him who had commanded it to stoop. Then Jesus said to it: Raise yourself, O palm tree, and be strong, and be the companion of my trees, which are in the paradise of my Father; and open from your roots a vein of water which has been hid in the earth, and let the waters flow, so that we may be satisfied from you.

cards.title: Abraham Breaking All the Idols Except the Largest One in Bereishit Rabbah
cards.note: Surah 21:51–67 narrates Abraham breaking his people's idols into pieces except the largest statue and telling his accusers that the largest idol did it and they should ask the statues if they can speak, matching Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators hold that the Quran restores the historical account of young Abraham's confrontation with his father's idolatrous community in Mesopotamia.
discussion.reply: Genesis 11:28–31 states that Terah and Abram departed from Ur of the Chaldees (`Ur Kasdim`). Because the Hebrew noun `ur` also means fire, Second Temple and rabbinic exegetes (Jubilees 12; Bereishit Rabbah 38:13) crafted a midrashic story in which Abraham breaks his father's idols, blames the largest statue, and is cast into Nimrod's furnace (`ur`).

[52] (Remember) when he said to his father and his people: ‘What are these images which you are devoted to?’ [53] They said, ‘We found our fathers serving them.’ [54] He said, ‘Certainly you and your fathers were clearly astray.’ [55] They said, ‘Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of those who jest?’ [56] He said, ‘No! sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.en: One time, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to him: ‘Here, offer it before them.’ He arose, took a club in his hand, shattered all the idols, and placed the club in the hand of the largest among them. When his father came, he said to him: ‘Who did this to them?’ He said to him: ‘I will not lie to you, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to me: Here, offer it before them. I offered it before them. This one [idol] said: I shall eat first, and another one said: I shall eat first. This big idol, who was standing among them, got up and took the club and shattered them.’ He [Teraḥ] said to him: ‘What, are you mocking me? Are they sentient at all?’ He said to him: ‘Do your ears not hear what your mouth is saying?’ He [Teraḥ] took him and handed him over to Nimrod.

cards.quranAr: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ رُشۡدَهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ ﴿51﴾ إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ ﴿52﴾ قَالُواْ وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ ﴿53﴾ قَالَ لَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُمۡ فِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٖ ﴿54﴾ قَالُوٓاْ أَجِئۡتَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ أَمۡ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّـٰعِبِينَ ﴿55﴾ قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمۡ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ ﴿56﴾ وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصۡنَٰمَكُم بَعۡدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدۡبِرِينَ ﴿57﴾ فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرٗا لَّهُمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ يَرۡجِعُونَ ﴿58﴾ قَالُواْ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ ﴿59﴾ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا فَتٗى يَذۡكُرُهُمۡ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ ﴿60﴾ قَالُواْ فَأۡتُواْ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡهَدُونَ ﴿61﴾ قَالُوٓاْ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلۡتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَـٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ ﴿62﴾ قَالَ بَلۡ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمۡ هَٰذَا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُمۡ إِن كَانُواْ يَنطِقُونَ ﴿63﴾ فَرَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّكُمۡ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ ﴿64﴾ ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمۡ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ ﴿65﴾ قَالَ أَفَتَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ شَيۡـٔٗا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ ﴿66﴾ أُفّٖ لَّكُمۡ وَلِمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ ﴿67﴾

cards.title: The Queen of Sheba Taking Solomon's Glass Palace Floor for Deep Water
cards.note: Surah 27:38–44 culminates with the Queen of Sheba entering Solomon's palace, supposing its polished crystal floor is a pool of water, and uncovering her legs, matching the Aramaic glass-house narrative in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators such as al-Tabari and al-Qurtubi treat the crystal pavilion and the uncovering of the Queen's legs as historical events from Solomon's royal court in Jerusalem.
discussion.reply: First Kings 10:1–13 and 2 Chronicles 9:1–12 record the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon without any mention of a glass floor, a hoopoe messenger, or the Queen lifting her garments over water. That sequence comes from the Galilean Aramaic Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2, an aggadic expansion of Solomon's court.

cards.quranEn: [38] He said, ‘Assembly! Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in surrender?’ [39] A crafty one of the jinn said, ‘I shall bring it to you before you (can) rise from your place. Surely I have strength for it (and am) trustworthy.’ [40] One who had knowledge of the Book said, ‘I will bring it to you in the wink of an eye.’ So when he saw it set before him, he said, ‘This is from the favor of my Lord to test me (to see) whether I am thankful or ungrateful. cards.title: Combining the Unblemished Red Cow and the Heifer for an Unsolved Murder
cards.note: Surah 2:67–73 merges two distinct Torah statutes into one narrative: the unblemished, unworked cow of Numbers 19:2–3 and the unworked heifer slaughtered for an unknown homicide in Deuteronomy 21:1–4, adding that striking the corpse revives the victim.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir recount an Israelite inheritance murder in which God commanded the sacrifice of a specific golden-yellow cow so that striking the slain man with its bone or flesh would bring him back to name his killer.
discussion.reply: In the Pentateuch, Numbers 19:2–9 prescribes burning an unblemished, unworked red cow to produce purification ashes for corpse-contamination, while Deuteronomy 21:1–9 prescribes breaking the neck of an unworked heifer in a valley to absolve a town of an unsolved murder. Neither statute involves striking a corpse with the cow to resurrect the victim.

cards.title: Iblis Refusing to Prostrate to Adam Because Fire Surpasses Clay
cards.note: Surah 7:11–18 narrates God commanding the angels to prostrate before Adam and Iblis refusing because he was created from fire whereas Adam was created from clay, matching the Latin Vita Adae et Evae 13–16 and the Syriac Cave of Treasures.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators present the command for the angels to bow to Adam and Iblis's boast of fiery origin over clay as the primeval account of Satan's fall at the dawn of creation.
discussion.reply: Genesis 1–3 contains no command for angels to bow to Adam and no dialogue with Satan about fire and clay. The narrative of God commanding the angels to worship the newly formed Adam comes from the apocryphal Life of Adam and Eve (Vita Adae et Evae 13–16), and Satan's specific boast that he is 'fire and spirit' refusing to bow to 'a thing of dust' appears in the Syriac Cave of Treasures.

cards.title: God Suspending Mount Sinai Above Israel Like an Overhanging Canopy (Zullah)
cards.note: Surah 7:171 states that God shook Mount Sinai above the Israelites as if it were an overhanging canopy (`zullah`) so that they thought it would fall upon them, matching the Talmudic aggadah of Sinai overturned above Israel like a tub in Shabbat 88a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir write that angels physically uprooted Mount Sinai and held it suspended over the heads of the Israelites until they accepted the covenant.
discussion.reply: In Exodus 19:17, the Hebrew phrase `be-tachtit ha-har` means 'at the foot of the mountain,' describing Israel standing at the base of Sinai. In Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a and Avodah Zarah 2b, third-century amora Rav Avdimi bar Hama homiletically renders `tachtit` as 'beneath' to picture the mountain held overhead like an upturned cask (`gigit`).

cards.title: Mary Accused by Her People and Addressed as Sister of Aaron
cards.note: In Surah 19:27–28, Mary's people accuse her over her child and address her as 'Sister of Aaron' ('daughter of Imran' in 66:12), combining Protevangelium of James 15 with Miriam, sister of Aaron and daughter of Amram, in Exodus 15:20 and Numbers 26:59.

discussion.view: Muslim traditions (Sahih Muslim 2135) and classical commentators explain that Mary was called 'Sister of Aaron' either figuratively after a righteous Israelite man or because she belonged to the Levitical lineage of Aaron.
discussion.reply: In Hebrew and Arabic (`Maryam`), Mary Mother of Jesus and Miriam of the Exodus share the same name. The Quran calls Jesus's mother both 'Sister of Aaron' (19:28) and 'daughter of Imran' (66:12; 3:35), matching the biblical family triad of Miriam—daughter of Amram (`Imran`) and sister of Aaron in Numbers 26:59 and Exodus 15:20—who lived over a millennium before first-century Mary.

cards.title: Wife of Imran Dedicating Mary to the Temple and Angels Bringing Her Food
cards.note: Surah 3:35–37 narrates the wife of Imran vowing her unborn child to the sanctuary, naming her Mary, and Zachariah finding miraculous food with her in the prayer chamber, matching Anna's vow and Mary's temple upbringing in Protevangelium of James 4 and 8.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes regard Mary's dedication to the Jerusalem sanctuary under the guardianship of the priest Zachariah and her miraculous out-of-season provisions as revealed prophetic biography.
discussion.reply: Under Mosaic law (Numbers 3:10; 18:1–7), residency and service inside the Temple sanctuary were restricted to male Levites and Aaronic priests, and canonical Gospels place Mary at home in Nazareth (Luke 1:26–28). The story of Mary's mother vowing her unborn child to the Temple and Mary living inside the sanctuary fed by an angel originates in the mid-second-century Greek Protevangelium of James 4:1 and 8:1.

cards.title: Waking After Centuries and Sending an Ancient Silver Coin to Buy Bread
cards.note: Surah 18:19–20 recounts the youths waking in their cave, supposing they slept a day, and sending one companion with their silver coin (`wariqikum`) to the city to buy food discreetly, matching the Syriac and Latin Seven Sleepers of Ephesus homilies.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir recount that the Companions of the Cave fled an idolatrous Roman emperor and were miraculously preserved in sleep for over three centuries as a sign of bodily resurrection.
discussion.reply: The narrative of Christian youths hiding in a cave near Ephesus under Emperor Decius (AD 249–251), waking under the Christian emperor Theodosius II (AD 408–450), and sending a companion into town with obsolete silver coins was a famous fifth- and sixth-century Christian hagiography preserved in the Syriac homilies of Jacob of Serugh (d. 521) and Gregory of Tours.

cards.quranEn: [19] So We raised them up (again) that they might ask questions among themselves. A speaker among them said, ‘How long have you remained (here)?’ Some said, ‘We have (only) remained (here) a day, or part of a day.’ Others said, ‘Your Lord knows how long you have remained (here). So send one of you with this paper (money) of yours to the city, and let him see which (part) of it (has the) purest food, and let him bring you a supply of it. But let him be astute, and let no one realize (who) you (are). [20] Surely they – if they become aware of you – they will stone you, or make you return to their creed, and then you will never prosper.’

sources.en: One of the youths, named Yamlikhā, goes down to the city to assess the situation and buy food. As the young man enters Ephesus, he is startled by the sign of the cross on the city's gates; when he tries to buy bread, the locals are astounded by the old-fashioned coins he is trying to use and think that has found a hoard. When the news reaches the city's bishop, he summons the young man and inquires about his identity; when the young man relates that he and his companions hid during the time of Decius, the whole city rushes to the cave, to see them.

cards.title: Korah (Qarun) Whose Treasure Keys Burdened a Troop of Men in Sanhedrin 110a
cards.note: Surah 28:76–82 states that Qarun (Korah) among the people of Moses possessed treasures whose keys burdened a company of strong men before the earth swallowed him, matching Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a and Pesachim 119a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators explain that God granted Qarun vast wealth among the Israelites in Egypt or the wilderness, and al-Tabari transmits reports that his leather treasury keys required dozens of mule-loads to carry.
discussion.reply: In Numbers 16:1–33, Korah leads a Levitical priesthood dispute against Moses and Aaron without any mention of vast monetary wealth or heavy treasury keys. The detail that the keys (`aklidei`) to Korah's treasuries were a load requiring three hundred white mules originates in the rabbinic aggadah of Rabbi Levi in Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 110a and Pesachim 119a.

cards.quranEn: [76] Surely Qārūn was one of the people of Moses, and acted oppressively toward them. We had given him treasures, the keys of which would indeed have been a burden for a group (of men) endowed with strength. (Remember) when his people said to him, ‘Do not gloat! Surely God does not love those who gloat. [77] But seek the Home of the Hereafter by means of what God has given you, and do not forget your portion of this world. Do good, as God has done good to you, and do not seek to foment corruption on the earth. Surely God does not love the fomenters of corruption.’ [78] He said, ‘I have been given it only because of the knowledge (that is) in me.’ Did he not know that God had destroyed those of the generations before him who were stronger than him and had accumulated more? The sinners will not be questioned about their sins. [79] So he went forth to his people in his splendor. Those who desired this present life said, ‘Would that we had the same as what has been given to Qārūn! Surely he is indeed the possessor of great good luck.’ [80] But those to whom knowledge had been given said, ‘Woe to you! The reward of God is better for the one who believes and does righteousness. But no one will obtain it except the patient.’ [81] So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, and he had no cohort to help him, other than God, and he was not one of those who could help themselves. [82] In the morning those who had longed (to be in) his place the day before were saying, ‘Woe (to Qārūn)! Surely God extends (His) provision to whomever He pleases of His servants, and restricts (it). If God had not bestowed favor on us, He would indeed have caused (the earth) to swallow us (too). Woe to him! The disbelievers will not prosper.’
quranHighlights: Surely Qārūn was one of the people of Moses, and acted oppressively toward them. We had given him treasures, the keys of which would indeed have been a burden for a group (of men) endowed with strength.

cards.quranAr: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ ﴿76﴾ وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ ﴿77﴾ قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةٗ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعٗاۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ ﴿78﴾ فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٖ ﴿79﴾ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ وَيۡلَكُمۡ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرٞ لِّمَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحٗاۚ وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّـٰبِرُونَ ﴿80﴾ فَخَسَفۡنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةٖ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنتَصِرِينَ ﴿81﴾ وَأَصۡبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوۡاْ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيۡكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَاۖ وَيۡكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ ﴿82﴾

cards.title: Angels Objecting to Man's Creation and Unable to Name the Creatures
cards.note: Surah 2:30–33 recounts the angels questioning why God would create a human who sheds blood, being unable to name the creatures when tested, and Adam naming them all, matching Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 17:4 and Talmud Sanhedrin 38b.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain that God informed the angels of Adam's appointment on earth and demonstrated Adam's divinely taught knowledge by having him name every creature before them.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 1:26 and 2:19–20, Adam names the animals without any angelic protest or competition. Rabbinic midrashim (Bereishit Rabbah 8:5; 17:4; Bavli Sanhedrin 38b) created this dialogue to explain why Genesis 1:26 uses the plural 'Let us make man,' portraying God consulting the ministering angels, the angels objecting to human sinfulness, and Adam surpassing them by naming the creatures.

cards.quranEn: [30] (Remember) when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Surely I am placing on the earth a ruler.’ They said, ‘Will You place on it someone who will foment corruption on it, and shed blood, while we glorify (You) with Your praise and call You holy?’ He said, ‘Surely I know what you do not know.’ [31] And He taught Adam the names – all of them. Then He presented them to the angels, and said, ‘Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.’ [32] They said, ‘Glory to You! We have no knowledge except for what You have taught us. Surely You – You are the Knowing, the Wise.’ [33] He said, ‘Adam! Inform them of their names.’ And when he had informed them of their names, He said, ‘Did I not say to you, “Surely I know the unseen (things) of the heavens and the earth”? I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.’

sources.title: Genesis Rabbah 17:4
sources.en: Rabbi Aḥa said: When the Holy One blessed be He came to create man, He consulted with the ministering angels. He said to them: “Let us make man” (Genesis 1:26). They said to Him: ‘This man, what is his nature?’ He said to them: ‘His wisdom is greater than yours.’ He brought the animals, the beasts, and the birds before them and said to them: ‘What is its name of this one?’ And they did not know. He passed them before Adam and said to him: ‘What is the name of this one?’ He said: ‘This is an ox; this is a donkey; this is a horse; this is a camel.’ [He then asked:] ‘And you, what is your name?’ He said to Him: ‘It is appropriate that I be called Adam, as I was created from the ground [adama].’ [He asked further:] ‘And I, what is My name?’ He said to Him: ‘It is appropriate to call you my Lord [adonai], as You are the Lord [adon] over all your creatures.’

He brought the animals, the beasts, and the birds before them and said to them: ‘What is its name of this one?’ And they did not know.

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin 38b
sources.en: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: At the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to create a person, He created one group of ministering angels. He said to them: If you agree, let us fashion a person in our image. The angels said before him: Master of the Universe, what are the actions of this person You suggest to create? God said to them: His actions are such and such, according to human nature. The angels said before him: Master of the Universe: “What is man that You are mindful of him? And the son of man that You think of him?” (Psalms 8:5), i.e., a creature such as this is not worth creating. God outstretched His small finger among them and burned them with fire.

sources.title: Genesis Rabbah 8:5
sources.en: Rabbi Simon said: When the Holy One blessed be He came to create Adam the first man, the ministering angels divided into various factions and various groups. Some of them were saying: ‘Let him not be created,’ and some of them were saying: ‘Let him be created.’ That is what is written: “Kindness and truth met; righteousness and peace touched” (Psalms 85:11). Kindness said: ‘Let him be created, as he performs acts of kindness.’ Truth said: ‘Let him not be created, as he is all full of lies.’ Righteousness said: ‘Let him be created, as he performs acts of righteousness.’ Peace said: ‘Let him not be created, as he is all full of discord.’

cards.title: Crucifixion Substitution: They Did Not Kill Him, It Seemed So to Them
cards.note: Surah 4:157–158 states that Jesus was neither killed nor crucified, 'rather it was made to appear so to them (`shubbiha lahum`),' matching the docetic substitution accounts in Irenaeus (Against Heresies 1.24.4) and the Nag Hammadi treatises.

discussion.view: Classical Sunni commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God cast the physical likeness of Jesus onto another person—such as a disciple or an enemy—who was crucified in his place while Jesus was raised bodily to heaven.
discussion.reply: First-century Christian, Jewish, and Roman sources (the Gospels, Paul, Tacitus in Annals 15.44, and Josephus in Antiquities 18.3.3) record Jesus's crucifixion under Pilate. The claim that a look-alike substitute was crucified while Jesus ascended unharmed originated in second-century Gnostic texts (Basilides in Irenaeus 1.24.4; Second Treatise of the Great Seth), which denied that a spirit could suffer in flesh.

cards.quranEn: [157] and for their saying, ‘Surely we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of God’ – yet they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it (only) seemed like (that) to them. Surely those who differ about him are indeed in doubt about him. They have no knowledge about him, only the following of conjecture. Certainly they did not kill him. [158] No! God raised him to Himself. God is mighty, wise.
quranHighlights: they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it (only) seemed like (that) to them
No! God raised him to Himself.

sources.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies
sources.en: Wherefore he did not himself suffer death, but Simon, a certain man of Cyrene, being compelled, bore the cross in his stead; so that this latter being transfigured by him, that he might be thought to be Jesus , was crucified, through ignorance and error , while Jesus himself received the form of Simon, and, standing by, laughed at them. For since he was an incorporeal power, and the Nous (mind) of the unborn father, he transfigured himself as he pleased, and thus ascended to him who had sent him, deriding them, inasmuch as he could not be laid hold of, and was invisible to all.

cards.title: Moses, His Young Servant, and the Salted Fish Reviving at the Spring
cards.note: Surah 18:60–65 narrates Moses and his young servant traveling to the junction of the two seas, where their dried fish revives and swims away into the water, matching the revived salted fish in Jacob of Serugh's Alexander discourse.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators and hadith (Sahih al-Bukhari 122) explain that Moses and his attendant Joshua set out with a salted fish in a basket as a divine sign to locate the sage al-Khidr at the meeting of the two seas.
discussion.reply: The Torah records the life of Moses and Joshua without any journey to the junction of two seas or a revived fish. In Late Antiquity, the episode in which a traveler's cook washes a dried salted fish at the Fountain of Life and watches it come to life and escape belongs to the Alexander Romance tradition, preserved in the Syriac discourse of Jacob of Serugh (d. AD 521; cf. the spring-washing variant in Talmud Tamid 32b).

cards.quranEn: [60] (Remember) when Moses said to his young man, ‘I shall not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, or (else) I shall go on for a long time.’ [61] When they reached the junction of them, they forgot their fish, (for) it had taken its way into the sea, swimming off. [62] So when they had passed beyond (that place), he said to his young man, ‘Bring us our morning meal. We have indeed become weary from this journey of ours.’ [63] He said, ‘Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Surely I forgot the fish – none other than Satan made me forget to remember it – and it took its way into the sea – an amazing thing!’ [64] He said, ‘That is what we were seeking!’ So they returned, retracing their footsteps. [65] And they found a servant, one of Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us, and whom We had taught knowledge from Us.
quranHighlights: When they reached the junction of them, they forgot their fish, (for) it had taken its way into the sea, swimming off.

cards.title: A Raven Sent to Scratch the Earth and Show How to Bury Abel's Corpse
cards.note: Surah 5:31 describes God sending a raven scratching in the earth to show Cain how to bury his brother Abel's corpse, paralleling Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 22:8 where the birds of the heavens and clean beasts bury Abel's body.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain that because Abel was the first human to die on earth, Cain did not know how to dispose of a corpse until God sent a raven to dig in the soil before him.
discussion.reply: Genesis 4:8–10 makes no mention of birds or burial instructions after Cain slays Abel. In fifth-century Palestinian Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 22:8, Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat addresses how Abel was buried by stating that the birds of the heavens and kosher beasts buried him, a midrashic motif that precedes the next verse's citation of Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 in Surah 5:32.

cards.quranEn: Then God raised up a raven, scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother. He said, ‘Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this raven, and hide the shame of my brother?’ And then he became one of the regretful.
quranHighlights: God raised up a raven, scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.ref: Bereishit Rabbah 22:8 (Birds of the Heavens Burying Abel)
sources.en: Who buried him? Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat said: The birds of the heavens and the kosher beasts buried him, and the Holy One blessed be He rewarded them with the two blessings that one recites over them – one for slaughter and one for covering the blood.
highlights: Who buried him? Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat said: The birds of the heavens and the kosher beasts buried him

cards.title: Jacob Commanding His Sons Not to Enter Egypt Through a Single Gate
cards.note: Surah 12:58–68 includes a specific command in 12:67 where Jacob tells his sons not to enter Egypt by one gate but by separate gates, matching Jacob's verbatim instruction in Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 91:2.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari, al-Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir explicitly state that Jacob feared the 'evil eye' (`al-'ayn`) striking his eleven handsome sons if they entered the royal city together through a single gate.
discussion.reply: Genesis 42–43 records Jacob sending his sons to Egypt to buy grain without any instruction about city gates or the evil eye. Both the command in Surah 12:67 ('Do not enter by one gate') and the exact rationale cited by Islamic commentators ('so that the evil eye will not have dominion over you') come directly from the fifth-century rabbinic commentary Bereishit Rabbah 91:2.

cards.quranEn: [58] The brothers of Joseph came, and they entered upon him. He recognized them, but they did not know him. [59] When he had supplied them with their supplies, he said, ‘Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I fill up the measure, and that I am the best of hosts? [60] But if you do not bring him to me, (there will be) no measure for you with me, and you will not come near me.’ [61] They said, ‘We shall solicit his father for him. Surely we shall indeed do (so).’ [62] He said to his young men, ‘Put their merchandise (back) in their packs, so that they will recognize it when they turn back to their family, (and) so that they will return (here).’ [63] When they returned to their father, they said, ‘Our father! The measure was refused us, so send our brother (back) with us, (and) we shall get the measure. Surely we shall indeed watch over him.’ [64] He said, ‘Shall I trust you with him as I trusted you with his brother before? God is the best Watcher, and He (is) the most compassionate of the compassionate.’ [65] When they opened their belongings, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, ‘Our father, what (more) do we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. We shall supply (food for) our family, and watch over our brother, and get an extra measure of a camel(-load). That is an easy measure.’ [66] He said, ‘I shall not send him with you until you give me a promise from God that you will indeed bring him (back) to me, unless you are surrounded.’ When they had given him their pledge, he said, ‘God is guardian over what we say.’ [67] And he said, ‘My sons! Do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates. I am of no use to you at all against God. Judgment (belongs) only to God. In Him have I put my trust, and in Him let the trusting put their trust.’ [68] When they had entered in the way their father commanded them – it was of no use to them at all against God, but (it was only) a need in Jacob himself which he satisfied. Surely he was indeed full of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know (it).
quranHighlights: And he said, ‘My sons! Do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates.

highlights: Jacob said to his sons: ‘You are mighty, you are handsome, do not enter through one gate and do not stand in one place, so that the evil eye will not have dominion over you.’
sources.orig: אָמַר יַעֲקֹב לְבָנָיו, אַתֶּם גִּבּוֹרִים, אַתֶּם נָאִים, אַל תִּכָּנְסוּ בְּשַׁעַר אֶחָד וְאַל תַּעַמְדוּ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, שֶׁלֹא תִּשְׁלֹט בָּכֶם עַיִן הָרָע.

cards.quranAr: وَجَآءَ إِخۡوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَعَرَفَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ ﴿58﴾ وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ قَالَ ٱئۡتُونِي بِأَخٖ لَّكُم مِّنۡ أَبِيكُمۡۚ أَلَا تَرَوۡنَ أَنِّيٓ أُوفِي ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَأَنَا۠ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡمُنزِلِينَ ﴿59﴾ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَأۡتُونِي بِهِۦ فَلَا كَيۡلَ لَكُمۡ عِندِي وَلَا تَقۡرَبُونِ ﴿60﴾ قَالُواْ سَنُرَٰوِدُ عَنۡهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَٰعِلُونَ ﴿61﴾ وَقَالَ لِفِتۡيَٰنِهِ ٱجۡعَلُواْ بِضَٰعَتَهُمۡ فِي رِحَالِهِمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَعۡرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ ﴿62﴾ فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيهِمۡ قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا ٱلۡكَيۡلُ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكۡتَلۡ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ ﴿63﴾ قَالَ هَلۡ ءَامَنُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ إِلَّا كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبۡلُ فَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ حَٰفِظٗاۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّـٰحِمِينَ ﴿64﴾ وَلَمَّا فَتَحُواْ مَتَٰعَهُمۡ وَجَدُواْ بِضَٰعَتَهُمۡ رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡۖ قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبۡغِيۖ هَٰذِهِۦ بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡنَاۖ وَنَمِيرُ أَهۡلَنَا وَنَحۡفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزۡدَادُ كَيۡلَ بَعِيرٖۖ ذَٰلِكَ كَيۡلٞ يَسِيرٞ ﴿65﴾ قَالَ لَنۡ أُرۡسِلَهُۥ مَعَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡتُونِ مَوۡثِقٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَتَأۡتُنَّنِي بِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَوۡهُ مَوۡثِقَهُمۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٞ ﴿66﴾ وَقَالَ يَٰبَنِيَّ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ مِنۢ بَابٖ وَٰحِدٖ وَٱدۡخُلُواْ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبٖ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٖۖ وَمَآ أُغۡنِي عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٍۖ إِنِ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِۖ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُۖ وَعَلَيۡهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلُونَ ﴿67﴾ وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَمَرَهُمۡ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةٗ فِي نَفۡسِ يَعۡقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَاۚ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذُو عِلۡمٖ لِّمَا عَلَّمۡنَٰهُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ﴿68﴾
